Hi Sam — thanks for the update and no worries. Good to know this is a firewall/proxy restriction rather than a scheduling mix. 

To make the next step smooth, I've attached a short preflight checklist (redwood_onboarding-checklist.pdf) you can hand to your infra team. Quick highlights to share with them:

- Whitelist domains: api.redwood.ai, auth.redwood.ai, storage.redwood.ai
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to the above domains
- Permit package registry: registry.npmjs.org (for Node) / pypi.org (for Python)
- If you use an egress proxy, allow CONNECT for those hosts and allow large request bodies for model downloads

If you want to try an async test first, here are two simple checks they can run from an internal host: 

1) curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health (should return 200 + JSON)
2) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEMP_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/engines (should list engines)

I've created two proposed rebook slots (PT): Wed 6/23 10:00–10:30 or Thu 6/24 09:00–09:30. Reply which works and we'll lock it in.

If you'd like our engineering CS lead to join for the rebook, I've CC'd Marissa who can take the deep-dive. We can also temporarily rotate a short-lived API key if your security policy prefers one-time keys for the session.

Attachments: redwood_onboarding-checklist.pdf (1 page)

Best,
Grace

Hi Sam — Marissa on the CS side. Sorry you ran into a blocker. A couple quick things to test when you have a minute:

- Can you paste the exact curl output (or attach trace_snippet.txt) from the failing registry download? That helps us tell whether it's an allowlist issue or proxy auth.
- If the curl to https://api.redwood.ai/health returns a 403, try a rotated API key — we can issue a temporary one (TTL 2 hours) and I can send it privately.
- If your proxy rewrites host headers, that can break our signed traffic; a passthrough or CONNECT is required.

If helpful, I'll generate a temporary read-only key and post it to your secure channel. Otherwise, pick a rebook slot from Grace's options and I'll join for the SDK install.

Attachments: trace_snippet.txt (20 lines)

Thanks,
